I have the highest priority at schools w and y (priority 1), and the second highest priority at schools x and z (priority 2). This means I am more likely to be accepted at w and y than at x and z if I propose to them. However, since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, y might have a high number of applicants, potentially making it more competitive despite my high priority there.

If I am rejected from x, my next best option is w, where I have the highest priority and a relatively high value (63). After w, I would choose z, as it has the same value as w but a lower priority rank. Lastly, I would choose y because, although I have high priority, the value is the lowest, and it is likely to be oversubscribed.

Therefore, my strategic ranking should prioritize schools where I have a balance of high value and reasonable chances of acceptance based on priority and competition from other applicants.
